content.text:
## Strengths

Genuinely good work on the hard parts. Specifically:

- **The throttle primitive is correct.** `tryAcquireThrottle` (`server/kv.js:28-34`) is a single `SET NX PX` round trip with no read-modify-write window. Two concurrent Vercel invocations cannot both win. The `result !== null` check is the right predicate for `@upstash/redis`. This is the thing most likely to be gotten wrong and it isn't.
- **The now-playing path is genuinely untouched.** `LeafletMap.jsx` only adds `!exploreMode &&` to the existing conjunction; the `MapController`/`AlbumBubble` block is byte-identical. `play(token)` still produces `{method:"PUT", headers:{Authorization}}` with no `body` and no `Content-Type`, and there is a direct test asserting the exact init object (`src/__tests__/spotify.test.js`, "play with no contextUri..."). `NowPlayingCard` swapping `controlMessage` → `displayMessage` is a no-op when `scopeMissing` is false. I looked for a regression here and found none.
- **The Task 7 abort fix is the right fix, done properly.** One `AbortController` per effect run cancelling both the in-flight fetch *and* the retry timer, plus a test that measures the max-concurrent-in-flight high-water mark rather than inferring it from call counts. That test would catch a real regression.
- **Guards run before `createRedisClient()`** (`api/geocode.js:11-26`) — a 405/401/400 never constructs an Upstash client. Small thing, deliberate, correctly commented.
- **Test quality is above the bar throughout**, especially `controllableFetch()` honoring `AbortSignal` semantics instead of faking them.
- **Docs are accurate.** The `Redis.fromEnv()` warning in `.env.example` and `server/kv.js:5-10` is exactly the kind of note that saves the next person an hour.

I also verified the one silent functional risk in `ArtistClusterLayer`: `react-leaflet-cluster@4.1.3` buffers `addLayer`/`removeLayer` and flushes on a microtask (`node_modules/react-leaflet-cluster/dist/index.js`), so markers appearing one at a time during background resolution *will* render incrementally while explore mode is open. That works.

---

## Issues

### Critical (Must Fix)

None. Nothing here corrupts user data, breaks the existing feature, or fails closed in a dangerous way.

### Important (Should Fix)

**1. The client cannot distinguish "no location" from "the backend is down," and the badge reports 100% either way.**
`src/useLibraryArtists.js:85-93` maps *any* non-200 and *any* network error to `{ status: "not_found" }`, then `:117` increments `resolvedCount`. Combined with the deferred finding that Redis calls in `api/geocode.js` are unwrapped, this is the concrete production failure mode: an Upstash outage (or a missing `REDIS_KV_REST_API_*` in a Vercel environment) makes every artist 500, so all 500 artists are marked `not_found`, `resolvedCount` reaches `total`, `LibraryLoadingBadge` *hides itself as complete*, and "Browse library" shows a confidently empty map with no error anywhere in the UI. The comment at `:76-83` reasons about not retrying, which is fine — but conflating a server fault with a per-artist negative result is what makes it invisible.
Fix: introduce a third client-side status (`"failed"`) that does not count toward `resolvedCount`, or at minimum wrap the Redis calls in `api/geocode.js` and return a declared `{ status: "unavailable" }` the hook can surface. Note the 401 branch is nearly unreachable in practice (App.jsx only mounts `MapView` after `/api/refresh` succeeded, so the `rt` cookie is always present), which is why I'm anchoring this on the 500 path.

**2. Every token refresh re-walks the entire library from zero.**
The effect at `src/useLibraryArtists.js:42` is keyed on `[token]`. Spotify access tokens live one hour; `MapView`'s 5s poll catches the 401 and `App.handleTokenExpired` sets a new token string. So roughly hourly, per tab: a fresh `fetchFollowedArtists` call, `setResolvedCount(0)` (`:139`), and 500 sequential `POST /api/geocode` invocations. With a warm cache each is one Vercel invocation + one Redis `GET` (the cache check at `api/geocode.js:30-31` precedes the throttle, so it's fast) — call it 30-60s of the badge visibly counting back up from `0/500`, and ~12k extra function invocations per day per long-lived tab. This is a whole-branch issue no per-task review could see, because it needs `App.jsx`'s refresh cadence plus the hook's dep array.
Fix: hold resolved results in a `useRef` map keyed by `artistId` that survives the effect re-run; hydrate `initial` from it and seed `resolvedCount` with the already-known entries, geocoding only what's still pending. Be aware `src/useLibraryArtists.js` sits at exactly 75.00% branch coverage, so the new branches need tests or CI fails.

**3. `resolved` cache entries live forever with no invalidation path.**
`server/kv.js:22-26` writes resolved entries with `options === undefined`. `server/geocode.js` picks `mbData.artists[0]` from a fuzzy MusicBrainz name search with no disambiguation — for common artist names, wrong matches are expected, not hypothetical. A wrong location is then permanent for every user of the app, fixable only by manually deleting keys in the Upstash console. `resolvedAt` is stored but never read, so it doesn't help.
Fix: a long TTL (e.g. `{ ex: 60*60*24*180 }`) on resolved entries. Locations don't change, but *our resolution of them* does, and a 6-month self-heal costs nothing (the spec's own concern is respecting upstream rate limits, and a 6-month re-lookup rate is negligible). This also blunts issue #4 below.

**4. The session gate does not do what the spec says it does.**
`api/geocode.js:15` checks only that a non-empty `rt` cookie *exists*. The spec justifies skipping decryption with "just confirm the caller is a logged-in user of this app rather than the open internet" — but a presence check confirms neither. `curl -H 'Cookie: rt=x' -d '{"artistId":"...","artistName":"..."}'` passes. The pattern was copied from `api/refresh.js:8-11`, but there the presence check is a *fast path* — the actual gate is `refreshSession()` decrypting the cookie two lines later. `geocode.js` copied the fast path and dropped the gate.
Concrete abuse, not just theory: because `artistId` and `artistName` are unvalidated and unlinked, anyone can `POST {artistId: <a real Spotify artist id>, artistName: <anything>}` and permanently pin that artist to a wrong location for all users — cache poisoning, made permanent by issue #3. Practical risk for a personal app is low (it's rate-limited to ~1/s and nobody is targeting it), but the fix is cheap: `openSession(sealed)` in a try/catch, which is what the spec's own rationale implies. If you'd rather keep it cheap, fixing #3 alone reduces poisoning from permanent to time-bounded.

**5. Under concurrency, the two-lock design systematically wastes MusicBrainz calls.**
Trace: client A acquires `throttle:nominatim` at t=0.4s (expires 1.5s). Client B acquires `throttle:musicbrainz` at t=1.15s, its MusicBrainz call returns at 1.35s, and `acquireNominatimThrottle` is denied because A's lock lives until 1.5s. B's MusicBrainz work is discarded, no cache write, and the client retries the *whole* artist including the MusicBrainz hop (`api/geocode.js:45-49`). Whenever MusicBrainz latency is shorter than the throttle interval — the common case — this is structural, not incidental: two MusicBrainz calls per resolution, against exactly the anonymous budget the spec exists to protect.
Fix, cheapest first: on Nominatim denial, cache the area name you already learned under a second key (`mbarea:<artistId>`, short TTL) so the retry skips the MusicBrainz hop. Alternative: one combined `throttle:geocode` lock with `px = 2 × interval` covering both hops — half the peak throughput but zero waste and no abandoned work.

**6. `retryAfterMs` is always the full window, never the remaining TTL — so a single user paces at ~half the achievable rate.**
`api/geocode.js:36` and `:48` both return `retryAfterMs: minIntervalMs`. Single-client trace: resolve at t=0.8s → immediately POST the next artist at 0.85s → MusicBrainz lock still held (expires 1.1s) → throttled → client sleeps the full 1100ms to t=1.95s, having only needed 250ms. Every artist costs two round trips and ~2.05s instead of ~1.1s. For the 500-artist user the prompt cites, that's ~17 minutes and ~1000 invocations, not ~8 minutes and 500.
Fix: in the deny path, `retryAfterMs = await redis.pttl(\`throttle:${service}\`)` (one extra Redis command, only on denials). Roughly halves first-run wall time. Add a little jitter while you're there — every throttled client currently retries on exactly the same 1100ms cadence, which self-synchronizes them into a lockstep herd. It's bounded and can't livelock (someone always wins the `SET NX`), but jitter is two lines.

### Minor (Nice to Have)

**7. `Number(process.env.GEOCODE_MIN_INTERVAL_MS ?? 1100)`** (`api/geocode.js:28`) — an env var set to empty string yields `0`, a typo yields `NaN`; both produce an invalid `PX` and a raw 500. `??` only guards `undefined`, and Vercel env vars set-but-blank are a real thing. Guard with `Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? n : 1100`.

**8. No type validation on `artistId`/`artistName`** (`api/geocode.js:19-22`) — `!artistId` passes objects and arrays, which then stringify into `geo:[object Object]` and the MusicBrainz URL. No injection risk (`encodeURIComponent` handles transport; the Lucene-query escape hatch via embedded `"` only lets an attacker pick a different artist, which they can already do), but `typeof === "string"` plus a length cap is one line.

**9. `ArtistMarker` with a null `imageUrl`** (`src/components/ArtistMarker.jsx`) — `img.src = artist.imageUrl ?? ""` sets `src=""`, which browsers resolve to the document URL and render as a *broken* image, not a blank circle. Spotify artists genuinely lack images. A colored `ACCENT` circle with the artist's initial would be strictly better than a broken-image glyph. (I confirmed the ledger's finding that coordinates are always present for `status: "resolved"` — that one really is a non-issue.)

**10. Preview/local/production share one throttle and one cache.** Vercel injects the same `REDIS_KV_REST_API_*` to all environments by default, so `vercel dev` on your laptop and every preview deployment contend for the same global 1 req/s budget as production, and write into the same `geo:*` namespace. Worth one line in `.env.example`; a `geo:v1:` / env-prefixed key namespace would be cheap insurance.

**11. The Nominatim lock key is untested** (`api/__tests__/geocode.test.js`, the "Nominatim-side throttle denial" case) — `expect(redis.set).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)` with no key assertion. See triage below.

---

## Deferred-Findings Triage

- **Explore mode unreachable while `status` is `"idle"`/`"error"`** — **must fix before merge.** This is the flagship feature of the branch being inaccessible in the single most common app state: opening the app before starting music. `MapView.jsx:172-186` returns a bare "Play something on Spotify" screen with no map and no button. **This is a plan defect, not an implementation defect** — the implementer followed the plan's snippet placement faithfully, and the plan never reconciled its JSX placement with the spec's "the loop runs regardless of explore mode so it's ready when you open it." Cleanest fix is to delete the `idle` early return and render "Play something on Spotify" as an overlay over the map; minimum fix is to render `LibraryLoadingBadge` + `BrowseLibraryButton` in the idle branch too.
- **`scopeMissing` warning invisible when nothing is playing** — **must fix before merge**, and it falls out of the above for free. Same root cause (`{track && <NowPlayingCard .../>}`), and it makes the migration note in the spec undeliverable for exactly the users who most need it: existing users, who often open the app with nothing playing.
- **`useLibraryArtists` swallows non-403 `fetchFollowedArtists` errors** — **fine to defer.** I traced the self-healing: `TOKEN_EXPIRED` resolves itself because `MapView`'s poll hits the same 401, refreshes the token, and the changed `token` re-runs the effect. Only a Spotify `429` on the single `/me/following` call leaves you stuck until the next token refresh (≤1h), which is low-probability and non-destructive. Lower severity than the ledger implies.
- **Redis calls in `api/geocode.js` / `server/kv.js` unwrapped** — **must fix before merge**, but as part of Important #1, not on its own. Unwrapped alone is survivable; unwrapped *plus* the client silently converting the 500 to `not_found` and reporting 100% complete is the bad outcome. Fix either end and the failure becomes visible.
- **Nominatim lock key never asserted in the test** — **must fix before merge.** It's a one-line change (`expect(redis.set).toHaveBeenNthCalledWith(2, "throttle:nominatim", "1", { nx: true, px: 1100 })`) on the highest-consequence subsystem in the branch. A regression collapsing both locks onto one key would silently double the rate at which you hit both upstreams, and nothing else in the suite would notice.
- **`ArtistMarker` null `imageUrl` guard** — **fine to defer**, though see Minor #9: it renders a broken image, not a blank one, which is slightly worse than the ledger recorded.
- **`useLibraryArtists.js` at exactly 75.00% branch coverage** — **fine to defer as a finding**, but treat it as an operational constraint on any fix you make to that file this round. Adding branches there without tests fails CI.

On the two adjudicated items: I'm not re-litigating either, and I found no unanticipated consequence of the `server/geocode.js` duplication — the divergence the author predicted (`acquireNominatimThrottle` + the `"THROTTLED"` sentinel) is exactly what materialized, and `src/geo.js` is untouched. `resolvedAt` is likewise harmless; the client ignores it. I'll note only that `resolvedAt` is stored but never read anywhere, so if you take Important #3 it becomes the natural basis for a "re-resolve entries older than N" story rather than dead weight.

---

## Recommendations

Ordered by value per unit of effort:

1. **Move the two overlays out from behind the `idle`/`error` early returns** (deferred #1 + #2). Highest user-visible impact in the branch, smallest diff.
2. **Add the one-line Nominatim lock-key assertion.** Free.
3. **TTL the resolved cache entries.** One line, and it simultaneously bounds the cache-poisoning window (#4) and the wrong-resolution problem (#3).
4. **Make backend failure distinguishable from `not_found`** (#1) — wrap the Redis calls server-side, add a `failed` status client-side that doesn't count toward `resolvedCount`.
5. **Return the real `pttl` in the throttled response** (#6). One extra Redis command on denials only, roughly halves first-run wall time.
6. Follow-ups that can land after merge: the token-refresh re-walk (#2), the wasted-MusicBrainz-call fix (#5), real session decryption (#4).

Two things worth raising with the author as design conversations rather than defects, since the learning goal is explicit in `CLAUDE.md`:

- **The global-throttle ceiling is the architecture's defining property.** One `SET NX PX` lock app-wide means total goodput is ~0.9 resolutions/sec *for all users combined*, so first-run time degrades linearly with concurrent users (10 simultaneous fresh users → each sees their library fill 10× slower). Warm cache mostly hides this after the early adopters, but it's the number to know. If this ever needs to scale, the shape that fixes it is moving resolution off the request path entirely — enqueue artist IDs, drain the queue with a single scheduled worker at a fixed rate, and let the client poll cache-only. That maps directly onto the Step Functions / streaming interests in `CLAUDE.md`, and it's the textbook control-plane (rate-limited resolver) vs data-plane (cache reads) split.
- **Request-scoped locks with abandoned work** (#5) are a recurring distributed-systems shape worth naming: whenever a unit of work needs two rate-limited resources acquired at different times, either acquire both up front or checkpoint the intermediate result. This implementation does neither, which is why the MusicBrainz call gets redone.

---

## Assessment

**Ready to merge?** With fixes

content.text:
## Strengths

Genuinely good work on the hard parts. Specifically:

- **The throttle primitive is correct.** `tryAcquireThrottle` (`server/kv.js:28-34`) is a single `SET NX PX` round trip with no read-modify-write window. Two concurrent Vercel invocations cannot both win. The `result !== null` check is the right predicate for `@upstash/redis`. This is the thing most likely to be gotten wrong and it isn't.
- **The now-playing path is genuinely untouched.** `LeafletMap.jsx` only adds `!exploreMode &&` to the existing conjunction; the `MapController`/`AlbumBubble` block is byte-identical. `play(token)` still produces `{method:"PUT", headers:{Authorization}}` with no `body` and no `Content-Type`, and there is a direct test asserting the exact init object (`src/__tests__/spotify.test.js`, "play with no contextUri..."). `NowPlayingCard` swapping `controlMessage` → `displayMessage` is a no-op when `scopeMissing` is false. I looked for a regression here and found none.
- **The Task 7 abort fix is the right fix, done properly.** One `AbortController` per effect run cancelling both the in-flight fetch *and* the retry timer, plus a test that measures the max-concurrent-in-flight high-water mark rather than inferring it from call counts. That test would catch a real regression.
- **Guards run before `createRedisClient()`** (`api/geocode.js:11-26`) — a 405/401/400 never constructs an Upstash client. Small thing, deliberate, correctly commented.
- **Test quality is above the bar throughout**, especially `controllableFetch()` honoring `AbortSignal` semantics instead of faking them.
- **Docs are accurate.** The `Redis.fromEnv()` warning in `.env.example` and `server/kv.js:5-10` is exactly the kind of note that saves the next person an hour.

I also verified the one silent functional risk in `ArtistClusterLayer`: `react-leaflet-cluster@4.1.3` buffers `addLayer`/`removeLayer` and flushes on a microtask (`node_modules/react-leaflet-cluster/dist/index.js`), so markers appearing one at a time during background resolution *will* render incrementally while explore mode is open. That works.

---

## Issues

### Critical (Must Fix)

None. Nothing here corrupts user data, breaks the existing feature, or fails closed in a dangerous way.

### Important (Should Fix)

**1. The client cannot distinguish "no location" from "the backend is down," and the badge reports 100% either way.**
`src/useLibraryArtists.js:85-93` maps *any* non-200 and *any* network error to `{ status: "not_found" }`, then `:117` increments `resolvedCount`. Combined with the deferred finding that Redis calls in `api/geocode.js` are unwrapped, this is the concrete production failure mode: an Upstash outage (or a missing `REDIS_KV_REST_API_*` in a Vercel environment) makes every artist 500, so all 500 artists are marked `not_found`, `resolvedCount` reaches `total`, `LibraryLoadingBadge` *hides itself as complete*, and "Browse library" shows a confidently empty map with no error anywhere in the UI. The comment at `:76-83` reasons about not retrying, which is fine — but conflating a server fault with a per-artist negative result is what makes it invisible.
Fix: introduce a third client-side status (`"failed"`) that does not count toward `resolvedCount`, or at minimum wrap the Redis calls in `api/geocode.js` and return a declared `{ status: "unavailable" }` the hook can surface. Note the 401 branch is nearly unreachable in practice (App.jsx only mounts `MapView` after `/api/refresh` succeeded, so the `rt` cookie is always present), which is why I'm anchoring this on the 500 path.

**2. Every token refresh re-walks the entire library from zero.**
The effect at `src/useLibraryArtists.js:42` is keyed on `[token]`. Spotify access tokens live one hour; `MapView`'s 5s poll catches the 401 and `App.handleTokenExpired` sets a new token string. So roughly hourly, per tab: a fresh `fetchFollowedArtists` call, `setResolvedCount(0)` (`:139`), and 500 sequential `POST /api/geocode` invocations. With a warm cache each is one Vercel invocation + one Redis `GET` (the cache check at `api/geocode.js:30-31` precedes the throttle, so it's fast) — call it 30-60s of the badge visibly counting back up from `0/500`, and ~12k extra function invocations per day per long-lived tab. This is a whole-branch issue no per-task review could see, because it needs `App.jsx`'s refresh cadence plus the hook's dep array.
Fix: hold resolved results in a `useRef` map keyed by `artistId` that survives the effect re-run; hydrate `initial` from it and seed `resolvedCount` with the already-known entries, geocoding only what's still pending. Be aware `src/useLibraryArtists.js` sits at exactly 75.00% branch coverage, so the new branches need tests or CI fails.

**3. `resolved` cache entries live forever with no invalidation path.**
`server/kv.js:22-26` writes resolved entries with `options === undefined`. `server/geocode.js` picks `mbData.artists[0]` from a fuzzy MusicBrainz name search with no disambiguation — for common artist names, wrong matches are expected, not hypothetical. A wrong location is then permanent for every user of the app, fixable only by manually deleting keys in the Upstash console. `resolvedAt` is stored but never read, so it doesn't help.
Fix: a long TTL (e.g. `{ ex: 60*60*24*180 }`) on resolved entries. Locations don't change, but *our resolution of them* does, and a 6-month self-heal costs nothing (the spec's own concern is respecting upstream rate limits, and a 6-month re-lookup rate is negligible). This also blunts issue #4 below.

**4. The session gate does not do what the spec says it does.**
`api/geocode.js:15` checks only that a non-empty `rt` cookie *exists*. The spec justifies skipping decryption with "just confirm the caller is a logged-in user of this app rather than the open internet" — but a presence check confirms neither. `curl -H 'Cookie: rt=x' -d '{"artistId":"...","artistName":"..."}'` passes. The pattern was copied from `api/refresh.js:8-11`, but there the presence check is a *fast path* — the actual gate is `refreshSession()` decrypting the cookie two lines later. `geocode.js` copied the fast path and dropped the gate.
Concrete abuse, not just theory: because `artistId` and `artistName` are unvalidated and unlinked, anyone can `POST {artistId: <a real Spotify artist id>, artistName: <anything>}` and permanently pin that artist to a wrong location for all users — cache poisoning, made permanent by issue #3. Practical risk for a personal app is low (it's rate-limited to ~1/s and nobody is targeting it), but the fix is cheap: `openSession(sealed)` in a try/catch, which is what the spec's own rationale implies. If you'd rather keep it cheap, fixing #3 alone reduces poisoning from permanent to time-bounded.

**5. Under concurrency, the two-lock design systematically wastes MusicBrainz calls.**
Trace: client A acquires `throttle:nominatim` at t=0.4s (expires 1.5s). Client B acquires `throttle:musicbrainz` at t=1.15s, its MusicBrainz call returns at 1.35s, and `acquireNominatimThrottle` is denied because A's lock lives until 1.5s. B's MusicBrainz work is discarded, no cache write, and the client retries the *whole* artist including the MusicBrainz hop (`api/geocode.js:45-49`). Whenever MusicBrainz latency is shorter than the throttle interval — the common case — this is structural, not incidental: two MusicBrainz calls per resolution, against exactly the anonymous budget the spec exists to protect.
Fix, cheapest first: on Nominatim denial, cache the area name you already learned under a second key (`mbarea:<artistId>`, short TTL) so the retry skips the MusicBrainz hop. Alternative: one combined `throttle:geocode` lock with `px = 2 × interval` covering both hops — half the peak throughput but zero waste and no abandoned work.

**6. `retryAfterMs` is always the full window, never the remaining TTL — so a single user paces at ~half the achievable rate.**
`api/geocode.js:36` and `:48` both return `retryAfterMs: minIntervalMs`. Single-client trace: resolve at t=0.8s → immediately POST the next artist at 0.85s → MusicBrainz lock still held (expires 1.1s) → throttled → client sleeps the full 1100ms to t=1.95s, having only needed 250ms. Every artist costs two round trips and ~2.05s instead of ~1.1s. For the 500-artist user the prompt cites, that's ~17 minutes and ~1000 invocations, not ~8 minutes and 500.
Fix: in the deny path, `retryAfterMs = await redis.pttl(\`throttle:${service}\`)` (one extra Redis command, only on denials). Roughly halves first-run wall time. Add a little jitter while you're there — every throttled client currently retries on exactly the same 1100ms cadence, which self-synchronizes them into a lockstep herd. It's bounded and can't livelock (someone always wins the `SET NX`), but jitter is two lines.

### Minor (Nice to Have)

**7. `Number(process.env.GEOCODE_MIN_INTERVAL_MS ?? 1100)`** (`api/geocode.js:28`) — an env var set to empty string yields `0`, a typo yields `NaN`; both produce an invalid `PX` and a raw 500. `??` only guards `undefined`, and Vercel env vars set-but-blank are a real thing. Guard with `Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? n : 1100`.

**8. No type validation on `artistId`/`artistName`** (`api/geocode.js:19-22`) — `!artistId` passes objects and arrays, which then stringify into `geo:[object Object]` and the MusicBrainz URL. No injection risk (`encodeURIComponent` handles transport; the Lucene-query escape hatch via embedded `"` only lets an attacker pick a different artist, which they can already do), but `typeof === "string"` plus a length cap is one line.

**9. `ArtistMarker` with a null `imageUrl`** (`src/components/ArtistMarker.jsx`) — `img.src = artist.imageUrl ?? ""` sets `src=""`, which browsers resolve to the document URL and render as a *broken* image, not a blank circle. Spotify artists genuinely lack images. A colored `ACCENT` circle with the artist's initial would be strictly better than a broken-image glyph. (I confirmed the ledger's finding that coordinates are always present for `status: "resolved"` — that one really is a non-issue.)

**10. Preview/local/production share one throttle and one cache.** Vercel injects the same `REDIS_KV_REST_API_*` to all environments by default, so `vercel dev` on your laptop and every preview deployment contend for the same global 1 req/s budget as production, and write into the same `geo:*` namespace. Worth one line in `.env.example`; a `geo:v1:` / env-prefixed key namespace would be cheap insurance.

**11. The Nominatim lock key is untested** (`api/__tests__/geocode.test.js`, the "Nominatim-side throttle denial" case) — `expect(redis.set).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)` with no key assertion. See triage below.

---

## Deferred-Findings Triage

- **Explore mode unreachable while `status` is `"idle"`/`"error"`** — **must fix before merge.** This is the flagship feature of the branch being inaccessible in the single most common app state: opening the app before starting music. `MapView.jsx:172-186` returns a bare "Play something on Spotify" screen with no map and no button. **This is a plan defect, not an implementation defect** — the implementer followed the plan's snippet placement faithfully, and the plan never reconciled its JSX placement with the spec's "the loop runs regardless of explore mode so it's ready when you open it." Cleanest fix is to delete the `idle` early return and render "Play something on Spotify" as an overlay over the map; minimum fix is to render `LibraryLoadingBadge` + `BrowseLibraryButton` in the idle branch too.
- **`scopeMissing` warning invisible when nothing is playing** — **must fix before merge**, and it falls out of the above for free. Same root cause (`{track && <NowPlayingCard .../>}`), and it makes the migration note in the spec undeliverable for exactly the users who most need it: existing users, who often open the app with nothing playing.
- **`useLibraryArtists` swallows non-403 `fetchFollowedArtists` errors** — **fine to defer.** I traced the self-healing: `TOKEN_EXPIRED` resolves itself because `MapView`'s poll hits the same 401, refreshes the token, and the changed `token` re-runs the effect. Only a Spotify `429` on the single `/me/following` call leaves you stuck until the next token refresh (≤1h), which is low-probability and non-destructive. Lower severity than the ledger implies.
- **Redis calls in `api/geocode.js` / `server/kv.js` unwrapped** — **must fix before merge**, but as part of Important #1, not on its own. Unwrapped alone is survivable; unwrapped *plus* the client silently converting the 500 to `not_found` and reporting 100% complete is the bad outcome. Fix either end and the failure becomes visible.
- **Nominatim lock key never asserted in the test** — **must fix before merge.** It's a one-line change (`expect(redis.set).toHaveBeenNthCalledWith(2, "throttle:nominatim", "1", { nx: true, px: 1100 })`) on the highest-consequence subsystem in the branch. A regression collapsing both locks onto one key would silently double the rate at which you hit both upstreams, and nothing else in the suite would notice.
- **`ArtistMarker` null `imageUrl` guard** — **fine to defer**, though see Minor #9: it renders a broken image, not a blank one, which is slightly worse than the ledger recorded.
- **`useLibraryArtists.js` at exactly 75.00% branch coverage** — **fine to defer as a finding**, but treat it as an operational constraint on any fix you make to that file this round. Adding branches there without tests fails CI.

On the two adjudicated items: I'm not re-litigating either, and I found no unanticipated consequence of the `server/geocode.js` duplication — the divergence the author predicted (`acquireNominatimThrottle` + the `"THROTTLED"` sentinel) is exactly what materialized, and `src/geo.js` is untouched. `resolvedAt` is likewise harmless; the client ignores it. I'll note only that `resolvedAt` is stored but never read anywhere, so if you take Important #3 it becomes the natural basis for a "re-resolve entries older than N" story rather than dead weight.

---

## Recommendations

Ordered by value per unit of effort:

1. **Move the two overlays out from behind the `idle`/`error` early returns** (deferred #1 + #2). Highest user-visible impact in the branch, smallest diff.
2. **Add the one-line Nominatim lock-key assertion.** Free.
3. **TTL the resolved cache entries.** One line, and it simultaneously bounds the cache-poisoning window (#4) and the wrong-resolution problem (#3).
4. **Make backend failure distinguishable from `not_found`** (#1) — wrap the Redis calls server-side, add a `failed` status client-side that doesn't count toward `resolvedCount`.
5. **Return the real `pttl` in the throttled response** (#6). One extra Redis command on denials only, roughly halves first-run wall time.
6. Follow-ups that can land after merge: the token-refresh re-walk (#2), the wasted-MusicBrainz-call fix (#5), real session decryption (#4).

Two things worth raising with the author as design conversations rather than defects, since the learning goal is explicit in `CLAUDE.md`:

- **The global-throttle ceiling is the architecture's defining property.** One `SET NX PX` lock app-wide means total goodput is ~0.9 resolutions/sec *for all users combined*, so first-run time degrades linearly with concurrent users (10 simultaneous fresh users → each sees their library fill 10× slower). Warm cache mostly hides this after the early adopters, but it's the number to know. If this ever needs to scale, the shape that fixes it is moving resolution off the request path entirely — enqueue artist IDs, drain the queue with a single scheduled worker at a fixed rate, and let the client poll cache-only. That maps directly onto the Step Functions / streaming interests in `CLAUDE.md`, and it's the textbook control-plane (rate-limited resolver) vs data-plane (cache reads) split.
- **Request-scoped locks with abandoned work** (#5) are a recurring distributed-systems shape worth naming: whenever a unit of work needs two rate-limited resources acquired at different times, either acquire both up front or checkpoint the intermediate result. This implementation does neither, which is why the MusicBrainz call gets redone.

---

## Assessment

**Ready to merge?** With fixes

**Reasoning:** The core engineering is sound — the distributed lock is correct, the now-playing path is verifiably untouched, and the test suite is better than most branches this size. But two things should not ship as-is: the flagship feature is unreachable whenever nothing is currently playing (a plan defect the implementer inherited, not an implementation mistake), and a backend outage renders as "your library resolved successfully, and it's empty." Both are small diffs; the rest — cache TTL, the real session gate, the throttle-efficiency work — is legitimate follow-up.

You are fixing findings from the FINAL whole-branch code review of the "library explore mode" feature branch. All 11 implementation tasks are committed; this is the last change before the PR.

## Project

`sound-map`: a Vite + React 19 SPA with Vercel serverless functions that maps the artist you're currently playing on Spotify. The branch adds a "Browse library" mode: a clustered map of every artist the user follows, resolved via `POST /api/geocode` (Upstash Redis cache + a `SET NX PX` distributed rate-limit lock in front of MusicBrainz/Nominatim), driven by a background loop in `src/useLibraryArtists.js`.

Work from: /Users/bert/github/sound-map
Branch: `library-explore-mode`. Do NOT switch branches.

## Read these first

- `/Users/bert/github/sound-map/CLAUDE.md` — project conventions.
- `/Users/bert/github/sound-map/.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-01-library-explore-mode/progress.md` — the run ledger, including which findings the author deliberately deferred.
- The files you'll be touching, in full, before editing them.

## The five fixes — the author explicitly chose this scope. Do these and nothing else.

### Fix 1 — Explore mode must be reachable when nothing is playing (highest priority)

`src/components/MapView.jsx` has early returns for `status === "idle"` (~line 172) and `status === "error"`, which render a bare "Play something on Spotify" / error screen with no map and no overlays. So `BrowseLibraryButton` and `LibraryLoadingBadge` only exist once something is playing — meaning the branch's flagship feature is invisible in the single most common entry state: opening the app before starting music.

The reviewer's preferred shape: **delete the `idle` early return and render its message as an overlay over the map**, so the map, the toggle, and the badge are always present. If that turns out to fight the existing layout, the acceptable minimum is rendering `LibraryLoadingBadge` + `BrowseLibraryButton` in the idle branch too — but try the overlay first, it's the better outcome.

The `error` branch: use your judgement. If the error is a hard auth failure, an inert map is arguably worse than the error screen; if it's a transient poll error, the overlay treatment fits. Say what you chose and why.

Note this is a **plan defect the original implementer inherited faithfully**, not their mistake — the plan's own JSX snippet put the overlays there. You are correcting the plan.

### Fix 2 — The stale-scope warning must be visible when nothing is playing

Currently the `scopeMissing` warning (a user whose session predates the `user-follow-read` scope, telling them to log out and back in) renders inside `NowPlayingCard`, which is itself gated on `track`. So the users who most need that message — existing users, who often open the app with nothing playing — never see it.

This should largely fall out of Fix 1. Make sure it actually does, and test it: the warning must be visible with no track playing.

### Fix 3 — A backend outage must not look like "your library resolved successfully, and it's empty"

`src/useLibraryArtists.js` maps *any* non-200 response and *any* network error to `{ status: "not_found" }` and then increments `resolvedCount`. Combined with `api/geocode.js` not wrapping its Redis calls, an Upstash outage makes every artist 500 → every artist marked `not_found` → `resolvedCount` reaches `total` → `LibraryLoadingBadge` hides itself as complete → "Browse library" shows a confidently empty map with no error anywhere in the UI.

Fix BOTH ends:
- **Server** (`api/geocode.js`): wrap the Redis calls so an Upstash failure returns a declared, documented response shape rather than a raw 500. Keep it consistent with the endpoint's existing `{status: ...}` vocabulary.
- **Client** (`src/useLibraryArtists.js`): a backend failure must NOT be recorded as `not_found` and must NOT count toward `resolvedCount`. Introduce a distinct status for it. Do not add retry-storm behavior — the existing reasoning about not retrying failures (see the comment around lines 76-83) is sound; the problem is only that failure is indistinguishable from a legitimate negative result.

Then make sure the UI is honest about it. `LibraryLoadingBadge` currently hides when `resolvedCount >= total`; with failures no longer counting, it would instead hang at e.g. `12/500` forever. That is arguably better than a false "done", but it is not good — decide on and implement coherent behavior, and explain your choice. Keep it proportionate; do not build an error-reporting framework.

### Fix 4 — Assert the Nominatim lock key

`api/__tests__/geocode.test.js`, the "Nominatim-side throttle denial" case, asserts `expect(redis.set).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)` but never that the second lock key is `"throttle:nominatim"`. A regression collapsing both locks onto `"throttle:musicbrainz"` would silently double the rate at which we hit both upstream services, and nothing in the suite would notice.

Add the assertion (e.g. `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith(2, "throttle:nominatim", "1", { nx: true, px: <interval> })`). Check the actual call shape in `server/kv.js` first so the assertion matches reality.

### Fix 5 — TTL the resolved cache entries

`server/kv.js` writes `resolved` entries with no TTL — forever. `server/geocode.js` picks `mbData.artists[0]` from a fuzzy MusicBrainz name search with no disambiguation, so wrong matches for common artist names are expected, not hypothetical. A wrong location is then permanent for every user, fixable only by hand in the Upstash console.

Give resolved entries a 180-day TTL (`60 * 60 * 24 * 180`). Locations don't change, but our *resolution* of them does, and a 6-month self-heal costs almost nothing against the upstream rate budget. Update `server/__tests__/kv.test.js` — there is an existing test asserting `redis.set` is called with NO `ex` option for `resolved` entries, which must now assert the TTL instead. Also check whether `CLAUDE.md` states the caching behavior and update it if so (it documents the 30-day `not_found` TTL).

## Explicitly OUT of scope — do NOT do these

The author deliberately deferred these to post-merge follow-ups. Touching them expands the diff and the review surface:
- The token-refresh re-walk (`useLibraryArtists`'s effect keyed on `[token]` restarting the whole loop hourly).
- Replacing the cookie-presence check in `api/geocode.js` with real session decryption.
- The two-lock design wasting a MusicBrainz call when the Nominatim lock is denied.
- Returning the real `pttl` as `retryAfterMs` instead of the full interval.
- An `ArtistMarker` fallback for a null `imageUrl`.
- Namespacing the Redis keys per environment.
- Anything about `server/geocode.js` duplicating `src/geo.js`, or the `resolvedAt` field — both were adjudicated by the author and are settled.

If while working you become convinced one of these is actually load-bearing for a fix you're making, STOP and report it rather than doing it.

## Global constraints (project-wide, binding)

- Follow TDD: failing tests first, then implementation, for each fix.
- The pre-commit hook runs `npx biome check . && npm test`. NEVER bypass with `--no-verify`. If Biome flags a file, `npx biome check --write <file>`, `git add`, re-commit.
- Commit messages follow `~/.git-template.txt`: **Why**, **How**, **Tests** sections. You may use one commit per fix or group them coherently — your call, but each commit must be self-consistent.
- Coverage bar (`vite.config.js`) is per-file: statements 90, branches 75, functions 100 for `src/**/*.{js,jsx}`, `server/**/*.js`, `api/**/*.js`, except the existing disallow-list. **Do NOT add anything to that disallow-list.**
- ⚠️ `src/useLibraryArtists.js` currently sits at exactly **75.00% branch coverage — the bar itself**. Fix 3 adds branches there. Every new branch needs a test or CI fails. Budget for this.
- `src/components/MapView.jsx` is at ~82% branches; Fix 1 will move a lot of JSX. Keep it above the bar.
- Test output must be pristine: no React `act()` warnings, no unhandled rejections, no leaked fake timers.
- **The now-playing path must remain untouched in behavior.** It is the app's existing feature and the final review verified it is currently byte-identical apart from the `!exploreMode` gate. Do not regress it. Do not modify `src/geo.js` or `AlbumBubble.jsx`.

## Verification

Run `npm test` and `npm run build` before committing. Report both results verbatim.

## Report Format

Write your full report to:
/Users/bert/github/sound-map/.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-01-library-explore-mode/final-fix-report.md

It must contain, per fix: what you changed and why, the design choice where you had one (especially Fix 1's error-branch treatment and Fix 3's badge behavior), and the covering tests with the exact command and its output. Plus: TDD evidence, files changed, coverage numbers for `src/useLibraryArtists.js` and `src/components/MapView.jsx` after your changes, self-review findings, and concerns.

Then reply with ONLY (under 20 lines):
- **Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT
- Commits created (short SHA + subject)
- One-line test summary + whether `npm run build` succeeded
- Your Fix 1 error-branch choice and Fix 3 badge choice, one line each
- Coverage for `src/useLibraryArtists.js` and `src/components/MapView.jsx`
- Concerns, if any
- The report file path

# sound-map

Map the music you listen to — see where artists are from as album art bubbles on a world map, updated in real time as your Spotify listening changes.

## Prerequisites

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) (v18 or later)
- A Spotify account
- A Spotify Developer app ([create one here](https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard))

## Setup

1. **Create a Spotify Developer app**
   - Go to https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard
   - Click **Create app**
   - Under **Redirect URIs**, add: `http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/callback`
   - Save your **Client ID** and **Client Secret**

2. **Create a `.env` file** at the repo root (this file is gitignored):

   ```bash
   cp .env.example .env
   ```

   Then fill in the values. `.env.example` documents each variable; you'll need
   your Spotify Client ID and Secret, a cookie key
   (`openssl rand -base64 32`), and the local callback/frontend URLs (already
   filled in for `vercel dev`).

3. **Install dependencies**

   ```bash
   npm install
   ```

## Running locally

Local dev runs the **same shape as production** — the static SPA plus the
`/api/*` serverless functions on a single origin — via the Vercel CLI:

```bash
npm i -g vercel      # once
vercel login         # once
vercel link          # once — link this folder to your Vercel project
npm start            # runs `vercel dev` on http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:3000, click **Login with Spotify**, and start playing
something.

> `npm run dev` still runs the Vite frontend alone (port 5173) for quick UI-only
> work, but `/api/*` won't be available there — use `npm start` for anything that
> touches auth or the explore-mode geocoding endpoint (`/api/geocode`).

## Running tests

```bash
npm test
```

## Deploying to Vercel

The app deploys as a Vercel project: the static SPA build plus the `/api/*`
serverless functions, backed by an Upstash Redis instance that explore mode
uses as a geocode cache and rate limiter. This section sets that project up
from scratch.

1. **Install the CLI and log in** (skip if you already did this for
   [Running locally](#running-locally)):

   ```bash
   npm i -g vercel
   vercel login
   ```

2. **Link the repo to a Vercel project**

   ```bash
   vercel link
   ```

   Linking writes a `.vercel/project.json` (gitignored) that records which
   Vercel project this local folder talks to — it's how `vercel dev`,
   `vercel env`, `vercel deploy`, etc. know where to read config and
   environment variables from. `vercel link` walks you through creating a
   new project or picking an existing one.

   For deploys triggered by `git push` rather than run by hand, also (or
   instead) import the repo from the Vercel dashboard: **Add New → Project →
   Import Git Repository**. Once imported, pushes to any branch produce a
   preview deployment, and pushes to the production branch (`main` here)
   produce a production deployment — see step 6.

3. **Register the production redirect URI with Spotify**

   The Spotify app from local [Setup](#setup) only has the local redirect URI
   registered. Go back to it on the
   [Spotify dashboard](https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard) and add the
   production callback under **Redirect URIs** too, e.g.
   `https://<your-project>.vercel.app/api/callback`. Spotify matches redirect
   URIs exactly, so it has to be the literal URL your deployment serves
   `/api/callback` from.

4. **Set environment variables**

   `.env.example` documents each one; set these by hand per environment
   (Preview / Production) in **Project → Settings → Environment Variables**
   in the dashboard, or with `vercel env add <NAME> <environment>`:

   - `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID`, `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET` — same Spotify app as
     local, from the Spotify dashboard
   - `COOKIE_ENCRYPTION_KEY` — generate a separate one for production
     (`openssl rand -base64 32`); don't reuse the local dev key
   - `REDIRECT_URI` — the production callback URL from step 3
   - `FRONTEND_URL` — the production origin (same as `REDIRECT_URI` minus
     `/api/callback`)
   - `GEOCODE_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` — copy the value from `.env.example`

   `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` and the Redis variables (next step) are auto-injected
   by integrations — don't set those by hand. Once everything above is set,
   pull it all into a local `.env.local` with:

   ```bash
   vercel env pull
   ```

5. **Provision Upstash Redis for explore mode**

   From the dashboard's **Storage** tab, add the **Upstash for Redis**
   integration (or `vercel integration add upstash`) and connect a database
   to this project.

   The integration injects Redis credentials into the project's environment
   variables under a **`REDIS_`** prefix: `REDIS_KV_REST_API_URL`,
   `REDIS_KV_REST_API_TOKEN`, plus `REDIS_KV_REST_API_READ_ONLY_TOKEN`,
   `REDIS_KV_URL`, `REDIS_URL`. That's why `server/kv.js` constructs the
   `Redis` client explicitly from `REDIS_KV_REST_API_URL` /
   `REDIS_KV_REST_API_TOKEN` instead of calling `Redis.fromEnv()` —
   `fromEnv()` only recognizes `KV_REST_API_*` or `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_*`
   pairs, and this integration sets neither.

   > The exact names can depend on how the integration is connected (which
   > product, project- vs. account-level). Don't assume the names above —
   > after connecting, run `vercel env ls` and check what actually landed
   > against what `server/kv.js` reads.

6. **Deploy**

   ```bash
   vercel          # preview deployment, own URL, doesn't touch production
   vercel --prod   # production deployment, promotes to the project's domain
   ```

   If the repo was imported via the dashboard (step 2), pushes do this for
   you automatically — any branch push makes a preview deployment, a push to
   the production branch makes a production deployment. `vercel` /
   `vercel --prod` are for deploying from your machine without waiting on a
   push.
